name: Tyrian Blue
lede: Tyrian blue is the blue sibling of Tyrian purple, the shellfish dye, and its best-known story is a religious one.

sections.title: Blue from shellfish
sections.body:
Finlay calls Tyrian blue one of the least kosher of colors [1]. Tekhelet, the blue thread of Jewish tradition, is made from a shellfish, though shellfish are forbidden food, which is why the dye sits on the fringe of what is permitted [1].

Paterson lists Tyrian blue among its blue names, in its list of blue names [2]. For the purple itself, see [[tyrian-purple]] [2]. Finlay sets the dye in a conference discussion of tekhelet, the modern effort to recover the ancient blue [1]. Because the dye comes from a living animal, it is a natural product that no pigment recipe in the books reproduces, and the page keeps to what Finlay and Paterson actually say [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #647B96 is a grey, dusty blue, far less saturated than the dye's reputation [3]. Neighbors are [[steel-blue]] and [[powder-blue]] [3]. Screen colors are approximate, and real dyed cloth varied [3].

origin.named_after: Tyre, source of the shellfish dye
